newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CIS, Iran demand push up Colombo tea prices.
newsitem.headline: CIS, Iran demand push up Colombo tea prices.

text.p: Heavy buying by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Sri Lanka's number one tea buyer, and the re-entry of Iran after a brief absence, pushed prices up at Wednesday's tea auction, brokers said.
All high and medium grown teas gained three to six rupees, while the better varieties of low growns were four to six rupees dearer, brokers Forbes & Walker said.
The anticipated gross sale average for the 4.8 million kg on offer was 102.30 rupees ($1.80), against last week's sale average of 101.87, Forbes & Walker said.
"There was a high intake from CIS and there were some purchases made on account of Iran, which was silent for the past few weeks," said Rohan Iddawela of Forbes.
Iraq, at one time Sri Lanka's top buyer, had yet to make a purchase from Colombo, but the market was eagerly anticipating Iraq's arrival very soon, Iddawela said.
Iraq was expected to resume buying from Colombo after last week's U.N.-sponsored oil-for-food deal.
The next auction is on December 10-11, with 4.9 million kg on offer. --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
